title: Indian Killed in Dammam Airport Attack, Embassy Confirms New Toll
excerpt: The Indian Embassy in Riyadh said Saudi authorities reported one Indian among two killed at Dammam airport on Wednesday night, with two Indians injured — separate from the Shaybah oilfield attack where an Indian was injured a day earlier.
body:
• An Indian national was killed and two Indians were injured in the Wednesday night attack on Dammam airport, the Indian Embassy in Riyadh confirmed on Thursday — a new development separate from the Shaybah oilfield incident.
  • At Shaybah a day earlier, drone debris killed a Filipino and a Nepali worker and injured an Indian and a Pakistani, according to the Saudi Energy Ministry.
  • Saudi authorities have not publicly identified who was responsible for the Dammam airport attack.
  • Indians in Saudi Arabia should follow embassy advisories: stay alert, shelter indoors during aerial attacks, and do not film interceptions or impact sites.

An Indian national was killed in an attack on Dammam airport in Saudi Arabia on Wednesday night, the Indian Embassy in Riyadh said on Thursday, in a new casualty report that goes beyond the Shaybah oilfield incident covered earlier. According to The Hindu BusinessLine, the embassy said Saudi authorities informed it that one Indian was among two people who lost their lives at Dammam airport, and two Indian nationals were injured.

"One Indian national was among two people who unfortunately lost their lives in the attack on Dammam airport yesterday night and two Indian nationals were injured."

— Indian Embassy in Riyadh, statement via social media

The embassy said it was ascertaining further details and contacting the affected families. It added, according to both BusinessLine and Livemint: "Our thoughts and prayers are with the family and loved ones of the deceased and we wish speedy recovery of the injured."

Two Separate Incidents, Two Days

The Dammam airport attack is distinct from the attack at the Shaybah oilfield. BusinessLine reported that the Shaybah incident happened on Wednesday, when a drone targeting Saudi Aramco's Shaybah oilfield was intercepted. The Saudi Ministry of Energy said falling shrapnel killed two residents, a Filipino national and a Nepali national, and injured two others, including an Indian national and a Pakistani national. That Shaybah report — an Indian injured, not killed — was the incident covered in earlier Videshi reporting.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=WMfdXPfp94U

At Shaybah, the interception caused a fire in a contractor's vehicle outside the facility's perimeter, but oilfield operations were not affected, according to Saudi authorities cited by BusinessLine. Livemint, citing the Saudi Energy Ministry, said the field has capacity to produce 1 million barrels of crude a day and operations were unaffected.

Keeping the two incidents separate matters for families and readers tracking casualties. The Indian death reported on Thursday was at Dammam airport on Wednesday night, not at Shaybah. The total Indian toll described across the two embassy updates is one Indian killed at Dammam, two Indians injured at Dammam, and one Indian injured at Shaybah.

Context: A Wider Campaign Against Saudi Infrastructure

Both attacks come amid escalating drone and missile strikes on Saudi airports, energy installations and other critical infrastructure. BusinessLine said Iran-backed Houthi rebels have been involved in a prolonged campaign against the kingdom, but added that Saudi authorities have not publicly identified those responsible for the Dammam airport attack. Livemint said the Houthis had not immediately claimed responsibility, had been attacking Saudi Arabia from Yemen over the past few months, and this month repeatedly targeted Saudi airports.

Livemint also reported that the United States Department of State issued an ordered departure on Wednesday for non-emergency government employees and their family members in Saudi Arabia, with spokesman Tommy Pigott cited via X, and that the US Embassy in Riyadh had earlier urged extreme caution when using airports in the kingdom due to attacks from the Houthis.

BusinessLine noted an earlier incident this month in which an Indian national was killed and several others were injured in an attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh. India has strongly condemned attacks on Saudi Arabia, particularly those targeting civilian facilities and infrastructure, and called for an immediate end to hostilities, according to BusinessLine.

What Indian Nationals in Saudi Arabia Should Do

Saudi Arabia is home to approximately 2.74 million Indian nationals, according to BusinessLine, working across sectors and forming one of the largest expatriate communities in the kingdom. That scale is why each new casualty report draws close attention from families in India and in the Gulf.

The Indian Embassy has issued advisories urging Indian nationals in Saudi Arabia to remain alert, follow instructions issued by local authorities and take shelter indoors during aerial attacks, BusinessLine reported. It has also cautioned them against filming or sharing images and videos of drone or missile interceptions and their impact sites, warning of possible legal consequences under Saudi law.

Further details on the Dammam victims, including identities and repatriation arrangements, had not been released in the reports available at publication. The embassy said it would provide assistance and remained in touch with Saudi authorities on the Shaybah case, and was contacting families in the Dammam case.
